title: hello-channel-imessage — a daemon that owns your Messages app (target: channel)

beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: “Watches the local chat.db, runs one model turn per message, replies via AppleScript.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env for the daemon beats — three levels up from a channel starter.

groups.title: Beat 1 · The spec: an agent, a channel, a routing key

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape
beats.cue: “Two lines: what it's called, and the long-running daemon spine to compile.”

beats.label: Add the agent
beats.cue: “Reply concisely (1-2 sentences)” — the instructions are written for a phone screen.

beats.label: Give it one tool
beats.cue: “You may use the Read filesystem tool to ground answers in repo state.” One tool, read-only.

beats.label: Wire the channel
beats.cue: Two words — imessage: {} — and no tokens, no app to register, no webhook URL to hand a platform. The platform is this Mac.

beats.label: Key sessions by user
beats.cue: sessionKey: user — one continuous conversation per contact, not one per message.

beats.label: Scope the permissions
beats.cue: Read is pre-approved, so an unattended daemon never parks a turn waiting for a human.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “Parse plus the IR passes the compile path skips, plus a scope audit — nothing emitted.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “The spec is sugar — this JSON is what the compiler sees: the agent, the channel, the routing.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target channel (channels.imessage, routing.sessionKey user)

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it: GREEN, with no key in the room.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (4 anchors); install ok; boot gated (boot reached its spec env refs gate). --check also runs `bun install --cwd live/dist`, which the poll beat below reads from.

beats.label: Open the emitted daemon
beats.cue: Eighteen lines of YAML became five files: daemon, gateway, session router, agent, README.

beats.label: Find the routing key in the bundle
beats.cue: “sessionKey: user” lowered to a sha256 of adapter:workspace:user — stable across restarts.

verify.note: 5 matching lines — deriveSessionId hashes the routing key into a stable sess_<16hex>

beats.label: Ask run to run it
beats.cue: “run is the cli/browser REPL.” A channel is a daemon — every other shape ships as a bundle.

verify.note: deliberate rejection — `crewhaus run supports target: cli or browser (got "channel")`

beats.label: Boot it with the key taken away
beats.cue: It names the credential it wants before it opens a socket, then exits 2. (env -u scrubs what Setup sourced, so the gate shows on camera either way.)

verify.note: designed refusal — `[daemon] missing required env vars: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; the emitted gate is the first statement in daemon.ts, above any adapter construction

beats.label: Give it a key but not consent
beats.cue: The kill switch. The adapter refuses to even construct until you opt in to owning this Mac's logged-in iMessage account — exit 1, no socket, no chat.db.

verify.note: designed refusal — `IMessageAdapterError: iMessage adapter requires CREWHAUS_IMESSAGE_HOST_ENABLED=1 (opt-in to host's logged-in iMessage)`. The dummy key only clears the env-name gate above; nothing reaches a provider. Off macOS the same beat exits 1 on the platform check instead. Note the throw is at daemon.ts module scope, outside main().catch(), so it prints a raw Bun trace rather than a formatted failure report.

beats.label: Boot the daemon for real
beats.cue: [needs-key] Opting in is a whole extra env var, on purpose. It serves the gateway on PORT — 3000 by default. Backgrounded, so this same terminal can keep going.

verify.note: needs Anthropic credentials plus the host opt-in; prints the janitor report then `[daemon] listening on http://localhost:3000` and stays up. Full Disk Access (chat.db) and Automation (AppleScript send) are only asked for by an actual poll/send — the daemon's boot path touches neither, so macOS does not prompt here. Deps were installed by the --check beat. Re-take housekeeping: `kill %1` (or a fresh terminal) before a second take, or :3000 is still held.

beats.label: Ask why no conversation appeared
beats.cue: Because nothing polled. The daemon registers the adapter and serves the gateway; draining chat.db is a call you own, on whatever cadence you want.

verify.note: 4 matching lines, in the adapter's own words: "the adapter exposes `pollNewMessages()` for the host to call; the generated channel daemon does NOT run a poll loop, so the caller is responsible for driving polling on whatever schedule it likes." Verified against the emitted bundle: `grep -n poll live/dist/daemon.ts` matches nothing, so .crewhaus/sessions stays empty no matter who texts this Mac — the earlier `ls .crewhaus/sessions` beat promised a payoff the bundle cannot deliver and was replaced by this one.

groups.title: One more thing · no app to register

beats.label: Try to provision a platform app
beats.cue: Slack, Telegram and Discord need an app registered. iMessage's platform is already on the desk.

verify.note: deliberate rejection — `the spec's channels block configures none of: slack, telegram, discord (imessage is configured but not supported by this command)`

beats.label: Find the adapter you never wired
beats.cue: An import, a constructor, one registration line, one gateway entry — the rest of the spine is shared.

verify.note: 6 matching lines: the @crewhaus/channel-adapter-imessage import, createIMessageAdapter, registerChannelAdapter, and the gateway's adapter map
